1: # opencode-container
2: 
3: Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.
4: 
5: ## Quickstart
6: 
7: **Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).
8: 
9: ```bash
10: make build
11: make serve
12: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
13: ```
14: 
15: That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
16: 
17: ## Containers
18: 
19: | Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Purpose |
20: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
21: | `opencode-serve` | `serve.dockerfile` | `serve` | 4096 | — | Headless HTTP server: web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc. Starts with an initialized git project. |
22: | `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
23: | `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
24: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
25: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
26: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |
27: 
28: ### Which container do I pick?
29: 
30: | You want to... | Use |
31: |---|---|
32: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
33: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
34: | Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
35: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` |
36: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` |
37: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` |
38: | Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |
39: 
40: ## Architecture
41: 
42: ### Why this design?
43: 
44: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements:
45: 
46: - **`serve` / `web`** are long-running HTTP servers. They bind to a port, persist data in Docker volumes, and expose health-check and API endpoints. They use `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for default flags, so `--help` passthrough works naturally.
47: 
48: - **`acp`** communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. To make it accessible over the network inside Docker, `socat` bridges the stdio protocol to a TCP socket (`socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 EXEC:"opencode acp"`). This allows external ACP clients (Cline, continue.dev) to connect without modifying the opencode process — it works on any port without opencode knowing about it.
49: 
50: - **`run` containers** (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`) are ephemeral. They clone a git repo, perform a task via `opencode run`, and exit. They use `profiles: [manual]` so they are never started by `docker compose up` — only via explicit `docker compose run --rm`. This prevents accidental startup of batch containers alongside long-running servers.
51: 
52: ### The profile/manual pattern
53: 
54: ```yaml
55: profiles:
56:   - manual
57: ```
58: 
59: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:
60: 
61: ```bash
62: docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
63: ```
64: 
65: This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.
66: 
67: ### Volume sharing strategy
68: 
69: All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:
70: 
71: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
72: |---|---|---|
73: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
74: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |
75: 
76: This means:
77: - Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
78: - Server and runner containers share the same config and history
79: - Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`
80: 
81: ### Base image
82: 
83: All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
84: - `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
85: - `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
86: - `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
87: - `socat` for the ACP bridge container
88: 
89: ### Network ports
90: 
91: | Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Auth |
92: |---|---|---|---|---|
93: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
94: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
95: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
96: 
97: ## Environment Variables
98: 
99: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
100: |---|---|---|---|---|
101: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
102: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
103: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
104: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
105: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
106: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
107: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
108: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
109: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
110: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
111: 
112: ### Env var security rules
113: 
114: - `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
115: - `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.
116: 
117: ## Commands
118: 
119: | Command | Description |
120: |---|---|
121: | `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
122: | `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
123: | `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
124: | `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
125: | `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
126: | `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
127: | `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
128: | `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
129: | `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
130: | `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
131: | `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
132: | `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
133: | `make lint` | `shellcheck ./*.sh` — static analysis on all shell scripts. |
134: | `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |
135: 
136: ### --help passthrough
137: 
138: Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:
139: 
140: ```bash
141: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
142: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
143: ```
144: 
145: ## Usage
146: 
147: ### Server containers (long-running)
148: 
149: ```bash
150: # Build everything
151: make build
152: 
153: # Start all servers
154: make run
155: 
156: # Start individual server
157: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
158: 
159: # Health check
160: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
161: 
162: # View logs
163: make logs
164: 
165: # Stop everything
166: make stop
167: ```
168: 
169: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
170: 
171: ```bash
172: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
173: ```
174: 
175: The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.
176: 
177: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
178: 
179: ```bash
180: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
181:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
182:   make plan
183: ```
184: 
185: The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.
186: 
187: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
188: 
189: ```bash
190: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
191: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
192:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
193:   -e ISSUE=42 \
194:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
195:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
196:   /script.sh
197: 
198: # Pass an inline command instead:
199: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
200:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
201:   -e ISSUE=42 \
202:   sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
203: ```
204: 
205: The worker (`generic-worker.sh`):
206: 1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
207: 2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
208: 3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions
209: 4. Exports `ISSUE` as an environment variable
210: 5. Executes the provided command (or exits with clone info if no command given)
211: 
212: **Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.
213: 
214: ## Testing
215: 
216: ```bash
217: make build    # Build all images first (required)
218: make test     # Run shellcheck + all integration tests
219: ```
220: 
221: The test suite (`tests/`) exercises:
222: 
223: | Test file | What it validates |
224: |---|---|
225: | `test-serve.sh` | `opencode-serve --help` returns help text |
226: | `test-web.sh` | `opencode-web --help` returns help text |
227: | `test-acp.sh` | socat binary is present, opencode binary is present |
228: | `test-generic-worker.sh` | Missing `REPO_URL` triggers error; clone-and-inspect on a real public repo |
229: | `test-issue-processor.sh` | Missing `GH_TOKEN` triggers error |
230: | `test-plan-issue.sh` | Missing `ISSUE_URL` triggers error |
231: 
232: ### Running individual tests
233: 
234: ```bash
235: bash tests/test-serve.sh
236: bash tests/test-generic-worker.sh
237: ```
238: 
239: ## Security Rules
240: 
241: 1. **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Always pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
242: 2. **Change the default password** in production: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` to a strong value.
243: 3. **`profiles: [manual]`** containers must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — never started by `docker compose up`.
244: 4. **Container entrypoints use `set -euo pipefail`** and validate required environment variables before proceeding.
245: 5. **Secrets never enter agent context** — runner containers pass tokens as env vars only, not as part of agent prompts.
246: 
247: ## Prerequisites
248: 
249: | Tool | Minimum version | Purpose |
250: |---|---|---|
251: | [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) | 24+ (Compose v2) | Container runtime |
252: | [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) | 2.x | GitHub authentication for runner containers |
253: 
254: Docker must be installed and the Docker socket accessible. The `gh` CLI is only required if you use the runner containers (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`).
255: 
256: ## Project Structure
257: 
258: ```
259: .
260: ├── serve.dockerfile          # HTTP server image
261: ├── web.dockerfile            # Web UI server image
262: ├── acp.dockerfile            # ACP protocol bridge image
263: ├── issue-processor.dockerfile # Batch issue processor image
264: ├── plan-issue.dockerfile      # Single-issue planner image
265: ├── generic-worker.dockerfile  # Generic clone-and-exec worker image
266: ├── generic-worker.sh          # Entrypoint script for generic-worker
267: ├── plan-issue.sh              # Entrypoint script for plan-issue
268: ├── process-issues.sh          # Entrypoint script for issue-processor
269: ├── docker-compose.yml         # All service definitions, volumes, profiles
270: ├── Makefile                   # All make targets (build/run/test/lint/clean)
271: ├── tests/                     # Integration test suite
272: ├── workflows/                 # Workflow harness definitions
273: └── AGENTS.md                  # Project-level agent instructions
274: ```
275: 
276: ## Dockerfiles detail
277: 
278: ### Base pattern (all containers)
279: 
280: ```dockerfile
281: FROM node:22-slim
282: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
283:     git ca-certificates [socat] [curl] && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
284: RUN npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
285: ```
286: 
287: ### Serve & Web
288: 
289: ```dockerfile
290: ENV OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=changeme
291: EXPOSE 4096
292: ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve"]
293: CMD ["--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"]
294: ```
295: 
296: ### ACP
297: 
298: ```dockerfile
299: EXPOSE 4097
300: CMD socat TCP-LISTEN:4097,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"opencode acp",pty,stderr
301: ```
302: 
303: No `ENTRYPOINT` — uses `CMD` directly so socat is the main process.
304: 
305: ### Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker)
306: 
307: ```dockerfile
308: ARG TARGETARCH
309: RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in ... download gh CLI ... esac
310: COPY *.sh /usr/local/bin/
311: CMD ["/usr/local/bin/script.sh"]  # or ENTRYPOINT for generic-worker
312: ```

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

```bash
make build
make serve
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.

| Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Volume sharing strategy

All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:

| Volume | Mount point | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
| `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |

This means:
- Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
- Server and runner containers share the same config and history
- Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`

### The workflows pattern

The `workflows/` directory contains reusable OpenCode workflow harnesses — shell scripts that orchestrate multi-step agent tasks in a structured, logged fashion. Each workflow:

1. Clones or assumes a repository working copy
2. Runs a sequence of steps (bash commands and/or `opencode` agent invocations)
3. Logs everything to a dedicated log file with ISO-8601 timestamps
4. Supports `--dry-run` for previewing without side effects

The main workflow:
- **`workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh`**: A full issue lifecycle workflow — checks for open issues, syncs main, fixes via agent, commits/pushes, resolves CI errors, reviews the PR, raises follow-up issues, and merges. Intended to run inside the `generic-worker` container.

Workflow harness scripts implement these functions:
- `log()` — ISO-8601 UTC timestamped logging to stderr + log file
- `run_step()` — execute a bash function step with failure handling, output streaming via `tee`
- `run_agent()` — pipe a prompt to `opencode run --format json` with optional `--agent` selector
- `catch()` — centralized failure hook that logs the step name and exit code

### Shell script robustness

Every `.sh` file in the repo root uses `set -euo pipefail` and validates required environment variables with descriptive error messages before proceeding. Shell scripts pass `shellcheck` at warning level with zero errors.

### Base image

All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
- `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
- `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
- `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
- `socat` for the ACP bridge container

### Network ports

| Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |

## Architecture

### Why this design?

OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements. Rather than crafting a single monolithic image, each mode gets its own Dockerfile. This gives us:

- **Isolation by purpose**: A `socat` dependency for ACP doesn't bloat the serve image. Git and `gh` CLI for runners don't affect the server image.
- **Independent lifecycle**: Serve/web containers run long-term. Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker) are ephemeral — they clone, execute, and exit.
- **Clean `--help` passthrough**: Serve/web use `ENTRYPOINT` so `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` works naturally. Runner containers use `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pointing to their shell scripts.

#### serve vs web — what's the difference?

Both `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web` run HTTP servers. The difference:

- **`serve`** (`opencode serve`): Requires an existing git-initialized project. The Dockerfile creates one at build time (`git init` + commit). Good for teams that want to control the project lifecycle.
- **`web`** (`opencode web`): Auto-instantiates a project on first load. Slightly more self-service for new users.

Pick `serve` for production/team setups where you mount your own project. Pick `web` for quick experiments.

#### Why socat for ACP?

OpenCode's ACP mode speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over **stdin/stdout** — it's designed for local processes, not network sockets. To make it accessible inside Docker without modifying OpenCode itself, `socat` bridges a TCP listener to the process's stdio:

```
TCP client → socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 → EXEC:"opencode acp" (stdin/stdout)
```

This is a classic Unix pattern: a small, trusted tool adapts a stdio protocol to the network. It works on any port, requires zero OpenCode changes, and the container is completely transparent about it.

#### Why the profile/manual pattern?

```yaml
profiles:
  - manual
```

Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:

```bash
docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
```

This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.

#### Why volume sharing?

All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:

| Volume | Mount point | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
| `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |

This means:
- Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
- Server and runner containers share the same config and history
- Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`

22: | `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
23: | `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
24: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
25: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
26: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |
27: 
28: ### Which container do I pick?
29: 
30: | You want to... | Use |
31: |---|---|
32: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
33: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
34: | Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
35: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` (`make process`) |
36: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` (`make plan`) |
37: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` (`make generic`) |
38: | Run a continuous issue-resolution workflow | `workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` |
39: | Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |
40: 
41: ### Managing repos for the issue processor
42: 
43: The issue processor (`process-issues.sh`) hardcodes target repositories:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: REPOS=(
47:   "tbrandenburg/made"
48:   "tbrandenburg/pyrag"
49: )
50: ```
51: 
52: Edit this array in `process-issues.sh` to change which repos it scans for open issues. Each entry is an `owner/repo` pair understood by `gh issue list`.
53: 
54: ## Architecture
55: 
56: ### Why this design?
57: 
58: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements. Rather than crafting a single monolithic image, each mode gets its own Dockerfile. This gives us:
59: 
60: - **Isolation by purpose**: A `socat` dependency for ACP doesn't bloat the serve image. Git and `gh` CLI for runners don't affect the server image.
61: - **Independent lifecycle**: Serve/web containers run long-term. Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker) are ephemeral — they clone, execute, and exit.
62: - **Clean `--help` passthrough**: Serve/web use `ENTRYPOINT` so `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` works naturally. Runner containers use `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pointing to their shell scripts.
63: 
64: #### serve vs web — what's the difference?
65: 
66: Both `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web` run HTTP servers. The difference:
67: 
68: - **`serve`** (`opencode serve`): Requires an existing git-initialized project. The Dockerfile creates one at build time (`git init` + commit). Good for teams that want to control the project lifecycle.
69: - **`web`** (`opencode web`): Auto-instantiates a project on first load. Slightly more self-service for new users.
70: 
71: Pick `serve` for production/team setups where you mount your own project. Pick `web` for quick experiments.
72: 
73: #### Why socat for ACP?
74: 
75: OpenCode's ACP mode speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over **stdin/stdout** — it's designed for local processes, not network sockets. To make it accessible inside Docker without modifying OpenCode itself, `socat` bridges a TCP listener to the process's stdio:
76: 
77: ```
78: TCP client → socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 → EXEC:"opencode acp" (stdin/stdout)
79: ```
80: 
81: This is a classic Unix pattern: a small, trusted tool adapts a stdio protocol to the network. It works on any port, requires zero OpenCode changes, and the container is completely transparent about it.
82: 
83: #### Why the profile/manual pattern?
84: 
85: ```yaml
86: profiles:
87:   - manual
88: ```
89: 
90: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
94: ```
95: 
96: This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.
97: 
98: #### Why volume sharing?
99: 
100: All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:
101: 
102: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
105: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |
106: 
107: This means:
108: - Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
109: - Server and runner containers share the same config and history
110: - Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`
111: 
112: ### The workflows pattern
113: 
114: The `workflows/` directory contains reusable OpenCode workflow harnesses — shell scripts that orchestrate multi-step agent tasks in a structured, logged fashion. Each workflow:
115: 
116: 1. Clones or assumes a repository working copy
117: 2. Runs a sequence of steps (bash commands and/or `opencode` agent invocations)
118: 3. Logs everything to a dedicated log file with ISO-8601 timestamps
119: 4. Supports `--dry-run` for previewing without side effects
120: 
121: The main workflow:
122: - **`workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh`**: A full issue lifecycle workflow — checks for open issues, syncs main, fixes via agent, commits/pushes, resolves CI errors, reviews the PR, raises follow-up issues, and merges. Intended to run inside the `generic-worker` container.
123: 
124: Workflow harness scripts implement these functions:
125: - `log()` — ISO-8601 UTC timestamped logging to stderr + log file
126: - `run_step()` — execute a bash function step with failure handling, output streaming via `tee`
127: - `run_agent()` — pipe a prompt to `opencode run --format json` with optional `--agent` selector
128: - `catch()` — centralized failure hook that logs the step name and exit code
129: 
130: ### Shell script robustness
131: 
132: Every `.sh` file in the repo root uses `set -euo pipefail` and validates required environment variables with descriptive error messages before proceeding. Shell scripts pass `shellcheck` at warning level with zero errors.
133: 
134: ### Base image
135: 
136: All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
137: - `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
138: - `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
139: - `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
140: - `socat` for the ACP bridge container
141: 
142: ### Network ports
143: 
144: | Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Auth |
145: |---|---|---|---|---|
146: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
147: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
148: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
149: 
150: ## Environment Variables
151: 
152: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
153: |---|---|---|---|---|
154: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
155: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
156: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
157: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
158: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
159: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
160: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
161: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
162: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
163: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
164: | `FLOWSH_LOG_DIR` | Test harness scripts (`tests/generic-worker/.harness/*.sh`) | no | `.flowsh/logs` | Override the log directory for generated flowsh harness scripts. Only relevant when developing or debugging test harnesses. |
165: 
166: ### Env var security rules
167: 
168: - `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
169: - `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.
170: 
171: ## Commands
172: 
173: | Command | Description |
174: |---|---|
175: | `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
176: | `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
177: | `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
178: | `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
179: | `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
180: | `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
181: | `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
182: | `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
183: | `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
184: | `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
185: | `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
186: | `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
187: | `make lint` | `shellcheck` on all shell scripts (root + tests). |
188: | `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |
189: | `make verify-quickstart` | Automated quickstart verification: build, serve, health-check, cleanup. |
190: | `make test-generic-worker` | Extended generic-worker integration tests (agent harness + repo inspection). |
191: 
192: ### --help passthrough
193: 
194: Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:
195: 
196: ```bash
197: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
198: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
199: ```
200: 
201: ## Usage
202: 
203: ### Server containers (long-running)
204: 
205: ```bash
206: # Build everything
207: make build
208: 
209: # Start all servers
210: make run
211: 
212: # Start individual server
213: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
214: 
215: # Health check
216: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
217: 
218: # View logs
219: make logs
220: 
221: # Stop everything
222: make stop
223: ```
224: 
225: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
226: 
227: ```bash
228: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
229: ```
230: 
231: The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.
232: 
233: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
234: 
235: ```bash
236: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
237:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
238:   make plan
239: ```
240: 
241: The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.
242: 
243: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
244: 
245: ```bash
246: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
247: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
248:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
249:   -e ISSUE=42 \
250:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
251:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
252:   /script.sh
253: 
254: # Pass an inline command instead:
255: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
256:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
257:   -e ISSUE=42 \
258:   sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
259: ```
260: 
261: The worker (`generic-worker.sh`):
262: 1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
263: 2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
264: 3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions
265: 4. Exports `ISSUE` as an environment variable
266: 5. Executes the provided command (or exits with clone info if no command given)
267: 
268: **Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.
269: 
270: ## Testing
271: 
272: ```bash
273: make build    # Build all images first (required)
274: make test     # Run shellcheck + all integration tests
275: make verify-quickstart  # Full quickstart verification (build → serve → curl → cleanup)
276: ```
277: 
278: The test suite (`tests/`) exercises:
279: 
280: | Test file | What it validates |
281: |---|---|
282: | `test-serve.sh` | `opencode-serve --help` returns help text |
283: | `test-web.sh` | `opencode-web --help` returns help text |
284: | `test-acp.sh` | socat binary is present, opencode binary is present |
285: | `test-generic-worker.sh` | Missing `REPO_URL` triggers error; clone-and-inspect on a real public repo |
286: | `test-issue-processor.sh` | Missing `GH_TOKEN` triggers error |
287: | `test-plan-issue.sh` | Missing `ISSUE_URL` triggers error |
288: | `verify-quickstart.sh` | End-to-end: `make build`, `make serve`, curl health-check, `make stop` |
289: | `generic-worker/run-tests.sh` | Extended agent harness + repo inspection (requires `GH_TOKEN`). Runs as part of `make test` when `GH_TOKEN` is set. |
290: 
291: ### Extended generic-worker test suite
292: 
293: The `tests/generic-worker/` directory contains an extended integration test suite for the generic worker container:
294: 
295: | File | Purpose |
296: |---|---|
297: | `run-tests.sh` | Test runner: invokes both harnesses inside the container |
298: | `.harness/agent_test.sh` | Bootstraps a custom agent and runs `opencode run --agent test` |
299: | `.harness/repo_inspect.sh` | Non-destructive: git log, file count, README check on a cloned repo |
300: | `agent/test.md` | Custom test agent definition ("test" agent) |
301: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow definition metadata |
302: 
303: These tests require `GH_TOKEN` for GitHub operations and are skipped by `make test` if the token is unavailable. Run them explicitly:
304: 
305: ```bash
306: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make test-generic-worker
307: ```
308: 
309: ### Workflow harness tests
310: 
311: The `workflows/issue-resolution/` directory contains a continuous issue-resolution workflow:
312: 
313: | Path | Purpose |
314: |---|---|
315: | `.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` | Full issue lifecycle: check issues, sync, fix, commit, review, merge |
316: | `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` | OpenCode config for the workflow (Context7 + sequential thinking MCP) |
317: | `.opencode/agent/review.md` | Custom review agent definition |
318: | `.opencode/commands/` | Command files: `prp-issue-fix.md`, `prp-review.md`, `commit-push.md`, `resolve-ci-errors.md`, and `ghar-*` variants |
319: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow metadata |
320: 
321: Run the continuous resolution workflow inside the generic-worker:
322: 
323: ```bash
324: docker compose run --rm \
325:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
326:   -e GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
327:   -v "$(pwd)/workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro" \
328:   opencode-generic-worker \
329:   /path/to/continuous-issue-resolution.sh
330: ```
331: 
332: ## Security Rules
333: 
334: 1. **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Always pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
335: 2. **Change the default password** in production: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` to a strong value.
336: 3. **`profiles: [manual]`** containers must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — never started by `docker compose up`.
337: 4. **Container entrypoints use `set -euo pipefail`** and validate required environment variables before proceeding.
338: 5. **Secrets never enter agent context** — runner containers pass tokens as env vars only, not as part of agent prompts.
339: 
340: ## Prerequisites
341: 
342: | Tool | Minimum version | Purpose |
343: |---|---|---|
344: | [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) | 24+ (Compose v2) | Container runtime |
345: | [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) | 2.x | GitHub authentication for runner containers |
346: 
347: Docker must be installed and the Docker socket accessible. The `gh` CLI is only required if you use the runner containers (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`).
348: 
349: ## Project Structure
350: 
351: ```
352: .
353: ├── serve.dockerfile          # HTTP server image
354: ├── web.dockerfile            # Web UI server image
355: ├── acp.dockerfile            # ACP protocol bridge image
356: ├── issue-processor.dockerfile # Batch issue processor image
357: ├── plan-issue.dockerfile      # Single-issue planner image
358: ├── generic-worker.dockerfile  # Generic clone-and-exec worker image
359: ├── generic-worker.sh          # Entrypoint script for generic-worker
360: ├── plan-issue.sh              # Entrypoint script for plan-issue
361: ├── process-issues.sh          # Entrypoint script for issue-processor
362: ├── docker-compose.yml         # All service definitions, volumes, profiles
363: ├── Makefile                   # All make targets (build/run/test/lint/clean/verify-quickstart)
364: ├── tests/                     # Integration test suite
365: │   ├── test-serve.sh
366: │   ├── test-web.sh
367: │   ├── test-acp.sh
368: │   ├── test-generic-worker.sh
369: │   ├── test-issue-processor.sh
370: │   ├── test-plan-issue.sh
371: │   ├── verify-quickstart.sh
372: │   └── generic-worker/        # Extended generic-worker tests
373: │       ├── run-tests.sh
374: │       ├── .harness/          # Test harness scripts
375: │       └── agent/             # Custom test agent definitions
376: ├── workflows/                 # Workflow harness definitions
377: │   └── issue-resolution/      # Continuous issue resolution workflow
378: │       ├── .harness/
379: │       ├── .opencode/         # OpenCode config, agents, commands
380: │       └── .made/
381: └── AGENTS.md                  # Project-level agent instructions
382: ```
383: 
384: ## Dockerfiles detail
385: 
386: ### Base pattern (all containers)
387: 
388: ```dockerfile
389: FROM node:22-slim
390: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
391:     git ca-certificates [socat] [curl] && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
392: RUN npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
393: ```
394: 
395: ### Serve & Web
396: 
397: ```dockerfile
398: ENV OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=changeme
399: EXPOSE 4096
400: ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve"]
401: CMD ["--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"]
402: ```
403: 
404: ### ACP
405: 
406: ```dockerfile
407: EXPOSE 4097
408: CMD socat TCP-LISTEN:4097,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"opencode acp",pty,stderr
409: ```
410: 
411: No `ENTRYPOINT` — uses `CMD` directly so socat is the main process.
412: 
413: ### Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker)
414: 
415: ```dockerfile
416: ARG TARGETARCH
417: RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in ... download gh CLI ... esac
418: COPY *.sh /usr/local/bin/
419: CMD ["/usr/local/bin/script.sh"]  # or ENTRYPOINT for generic-worker
420: ```
421:

423: 
424: MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
